gates.reason: Security-boundary tests verify the preregistration bridge has no filesystem, child-process, fetch, credential-path, or environment access and rejects altered definitions.
Tests pin the canonical definition digest, projection, semantics manifests, fingerprint factors, mutation rejection, receipt binding, and experimental parameters for reproducibility.
Test-only code is not shipped on a runtime hot path.

The bridge uses fixed command argv and static experiment configuration, performs no filesystem or network egress, accesses no credentials, and validates definition identity and digest before projection.
The preregistered subjects, treatments, budgets, checks, metrics, provenance-oriented capability semantics, fingerprint policy, pairing rules, and verdict parameters are digest-bound and immutable.
This is a small, fixed preregistration definition assembled at module initialization, not an ingest or request hot path.
Tests cover prototype-named keys and fail-closed handling of non-JSON values, cycles, sparse arrays, symbol keys, and non-plain objects at the canonicalization boundary.
Tests pin fixture and fingerprint digests and verify that only contract-declared set arrays are permutation-invariant.
Test-only canonicalization checks are not shipped on a runtime hot path.
Untrusted values are cloned into a null-prototype strict JSON domain; cycles, symbols, non-plain objects, invalid numbers, malformed Unicode, sparse arrays, and named array properties fail closed.
Canonical serialization, explicitly scoped set normalization, self-digest omission, and SHA-256 calculation are deterministic and preserve order where the contract assigns meaning.
Canonicalization performs bounded tree cloning plus sorting of declared set arrays, with no repeated external I/O, rendering, or per-request fan-out hotspot.
